title: What differs between well-mixed and viscous populations before well-mixed ones collapse?
question: F and F2 found that well-mixed populations die out sooner, but their population sizes were not more volatile before collapse. In the first 6000 ticks, before any population has died out, do well-mixed populations differ in birth rate, death rate, cause of death (killed, starved, old age) or offspring success?
background: F2 (seeds 100-115): extinctions 13/16 vs 7/16; the earliest extinction was at tick 7332; population CV over ticks 0-6000 was 0.073 in both conditions. All metrics here are measured over ticks 0-6000 only, so they precede the collapse. Offspring success is the fraction of agents born before tick 4500 that reproduced at least once before tick 6000. Seeds 500-515 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Before collapse, well-mixed populations have a lower birth rate per agent-tick
Before collapse, a larger fraction of well-mixed deaths are killings
Before collapse, a larger fraction of well-mixed deaths are starvation
Before collapse, fewer well-mixed offspring go on to reproduce
Third test: well-mixed populations die out sooner
